plan.chapterName: OpenStax University Physics, chapter 9: Linear Momentum and Collisions
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a three-dimensional drawing of a single cubic unit cell of a sodium chloride crystal set on a coordinate frame. Solid black axes emerge from a corner labeled 0 at the lower left, with x running toward the lower right, y toward the upper right, and z straight up, each ending in an arrowhead beside its italic label. Dashed orange lines trace the edges of the cube. Eight shaded spheres sit at the corners in two alternating colors, each tagged with a subscripted mass symbol. The green spheres are m_1 at the origin, m_3 at the far corner of the xy face, m_6 at the far corner of the xz face, and m_8 at the far corner of the yz face. The red spheres are m_2 out along the x-axis, m_4 out along the y-axis, m_5 up the z-axis, and m_7 at the corner diagonally opposite the origin. The alternation of the two colors around every face shows that no two like-colored ions share an edge, and numbering all eight corners while anchoring the origin on one of them supplies the labeled coordinates needed to work out the center of mass of the eight-particle cell.

Coordinates and colors: m1(0,0,0) Green, m2(2,0,0) Red, m3(2,2,0) Green, m4(0,2,0) Red, m5(0,0,2) Red, m6(2,0,2) Green, m7(2,2,2) Red, m8(0,2,2) Green. Colors: Green #7b9f35, Red #c73c3d, dashed lines orange #e66c3a. The alternating pattern ensures ions on the same axis or face diagonal differ from the origin ion, but body diagonal (m7) differs from origin (m1).
interactionPlan.notes: When 'inspectIon' (hover) is active, dim the opacity of all spheres that do not match the hovered sphere's color to 0.3, and display a floating text tag showing its coordinate (e.g., '(a, 0, a)'). When 'displayMode' is 'Calculation Data', change all spheres to a neutral gray, increase the size/weight of the m_i labels, and permanently show the coordinates next to each label.

Solution Define the origin to be at the location of the chloride ion at the bottom left of the unit cell. The figure shows the coordinate system.

A single unit cell of a NaCl crystal.

An illustration of a unit cell of an N a C l crystal as a cube with ions at each corner. Four green ions are shown and labeled as m 1 at the origin, m 3 at the corner on the diagonal on the x y plane, m 6 at the corner on the diagonal on the x z plane, and m 8 at the corner on the diagonal on the y z plane. Four red ions are shown and labeled as m 2 on the x axis, m 4 on the y axis, m 5 on the z axis, and m 7 on the remaining corner.

There are eight ions in this crystal, so N = 8:
